html:
SMTO-GWT-0087 — The Gateway's private files aren't protected the way they must be

GUID: 4e094512-2c84-54f0-8d89-6d1576d8ac07
Slug: gateway-private-storage-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • The Gateway keeps private files, such as its job records and security keys, that only its own user account may touch. Some of them have the wrong owner or permissions, so the Gateway won't use them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the Gateway is started by the same user account on that computer that originally installed it, not by an administrator or root account. Files created by another account have a different owner, and the Gateway refuses files it doesn't own.
  2. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to stop the Gateway and make its data folder readable only by that account. The Gateway refuses files other users could read, because they hold security keys and job records.
  3. If the data folder was recently copied, moved or linked to another place, put it back as a normal folder in its original location. The Gateway refuses linked or copied files it can't confirm are its own.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway starts and shows as connected in Settings › Setup › Gateways.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer; the details name the exact file. Don't delete the Gateway's data folder to get past this; it holds its pairing and job history.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway private-state access rejected a path because it is a symbolic link or has the wrong file type, a foreign owner, group/world permissions, multiple hard links, an invalid Windows ACL, or an oversized or changed record; a platform API failure can also prevent verification.

What this means

  • Private-state access rejected links, unexpected file type or owner, broad permissions, invalid ACLs, oversized/changed records or an invalid node identity; platform API failures can also prevent verification. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Private-state access rejected links, unexpected file type or owner, broad permissions, invalid ACLs, oversized/changed records or an invalid node identity; platform API failures can also prevent verification.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported path and exact failed ownership, ACL, type, link or record-bound check under the Gateway account; preserve data during repair.

How to fix it

  • Find the path in the Technical details (default jobs root is ~/.smto/jobs/<node>, or GATEWAY_JOB_DIR / GATEWAY_TLS_STATE_DIR when set). Stop the Gateway, then make the directory and files owned by the OS account that runs the Gateway, with mode 0700 for directories and 0600 for files (on Windows, an ACL limited to that user), and remove any symlinks or hard links; do not delete or regenerate the existing state.
  • Check the reported Gateway state path and private ownership/permissions. Stop the Gateway before repair and preserve existing state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing intended state passes private storage validation under its rightful owner.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
